quest.title: The Secret of Al-Ahmar
quest.description: Tirzad accidentally opened the hidden passage behind the mural. No one knows where it may lead...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

talks.objective: Enter the secret passage behind the mural

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon feels even smaller now that we've gotten closer... Paimon feels as insignificant as a grain of sand...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: That was also one of King Deshret's means of ruling. Building huge spectacles to instill the idea that his subjects are small and insignificant into them, thus achieving the objective of domesticating them.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: The act of using huge amounts of manpower to build such a spectacle in the desert is a testament to King Deshret's tyranny.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Beep... Bee-eep beep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! So Benben can even open a door this huge?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: It's difficult to say! Maybe it just opened on its own! It may... it might have nothing to do with Benben.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gah, why's he being so stubborn?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Then explain to me how this thing... Benben opened the door. What's the logic behind that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Paimon doesn't know either!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmm, Benben? What is it? Do you want to go inside? Is there something you're familiar with in there?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Beep...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: A grain of sand is insignificant, but an ocean of them possesses immeasurable strength. Researcher of blind faith, do you really have the courage to set foot into the sands?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: We're already here! So of course we must go inside!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Still, my researcher's intuition is telling me that the danger ahead is incomparable to the dangers we've faced so far!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: #I doubt I can trust either of you desert dwellers, so {NICKNAME}, I'm counting on you to keep me safe!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, it's just some differences of opinion. It isn't that serious, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Hmph! You don't get it at all! A collision of views in academics is no different from a battle!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sheesh, this guy's really getting more annoying by the minute!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So, are all of you done? It's not that easy to hold Benben back...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Benben really wants to go inside, huh? Let's stop delaying then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! These ruins are magnificent!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Those aren't ordinary ruins. If the records are correct, they should be King Deshret's Mausoleum. It's where the tyrant is buried.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Sh—should we still go forward, then?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: All questions have an answer, and all answers slumber here.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Hmph! I will do this, even if all I achieve is showing some ignorant mercenaries the error of their ways...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uh... {NICKNAME}, let's head over carefully!

talks.objective: Go to the Mausoleum of King Deshret

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: It's a pity that Ufairah will never get to see this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Ufairah? Paimon's never heard him mention that name.)

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Phew! Thank goodness Benben's alright... Seriously, stop rushing off so quickly! What if you got into trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Should that be called an injury or a malfunction?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Agh, does it matter? There aren't any doctors or technicians here anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We do have a bunch of angry adults, though.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Haha, you're absolutely right about that!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I'm not angry. This place is full of evidence! It will not take long to prove that I'm right. I mean, look at this huge coffin! Tsk tsk...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: ...Wait. What? How do we get this thing open?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't figure out if he's brave or cowardly...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: What are those?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The huge statues here... Don't they look like guards? They're so intimidating! Tirzad, Paimon thinks it's best if you don't touch anything here...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: They're just rocks. We have nothing to fear from rocks... Aha! There may be a mechanism around here somewhere... Let me take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: ...We should split up and search for clues.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: *sigh* Father feels so unfamiliar right now. What's going on? Benben, do you know why?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Bee-eep?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: The material I've gathered so far... They should be enough for two chapters... Wait, will that really be enough?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: #Oh! {NICKNAME}, as impressive as always! I'll definitely credit you if I'm able to publish my paper successfully.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Ahem, although what we're about to do is disrespectful, it's all done for academic progress. I promise it's not for selfish gain!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Wait! Huh? There's...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's nothing in here!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: How is this possible? But these diagrams... Wait, wait a minute. Let me think.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I get it now. This has to be an illusion.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Of course King Deshret knew that inquisitive researchers like me would come with the desire to get to the bottom of things and uncover all his secrets.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: So, of course he wouldn't let others get to them that easily. Thus, he built this huge mausoleum and prepared so many... doors, and rooms.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: He even went so far as to prepare illusions like this to mislead us.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: The most important things wouldn't be placed in such a conspicuous spot! Moreover, this place is too low, way too low...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: The real treasure is definitely higher up. It must be in a place closer to the sky...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: What utter nonsense.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Oh? Well, let's hear what you think, then!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I may not be able to say what exactly it's for, but I know for sure that what you say is untrue.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Hmph! Does someone like you even have the right to say that I only draw from the work of others? You don't even have the intelligence to use the work of others!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Indeed. But I am still convinced that you know too little about these sands.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Stop going on about the sands! What you see is the truth! J—Just you wait! I'll find solid proof that you can't refute!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Up! Let's go upward!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's find a way up. Paimon's worried that Tirzad will get himself into trouble if this goes on...

talks.objective: Find the way to the upper floor
Go to the highest floor of the Mausoleum of King Deshret

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Theoretically, this should be where King Deshret's "organs" are stored...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But just like before, nothing "physical" is stored here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Oh... I have a theory, but I need more evidence to prove it.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father, what do you think? I'm sure you know something, right? Even if you didn't tell me or anyone else...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: The stone slate is the key, but it cannot open all doors. Even the key must first receive "acknowledgment."

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Bee-eep! Beep—

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Oh, Benben's link to this place is obvious, but what do you mean, the stone slate must receive "acknowledgment"? That's just absurd.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Benben, who do you think is correct?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Now that I've calmed down a little, I can understand why Jebrael is challenging my views. You said that he was once from the desert...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Perhaps some experiences, maybe even verbal, have been treated as "knowledge." Not that they are true knowledge, of course, and naturally, there are no academic records of such things.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: His superstitions are understandable considering the society he lived in.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But Jeht, do you really think that Benben's... uh, "words," are worth believing? These are, after all, words that came out of nowhere instead of an actual academic researcher, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Huh? But Benben has helped a lot on our trip. As for you, Tirzad... You've been nothing but talk!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I doubt your speeches, high-flown though they sound, are even entirely correct. I get the feeling that my father knows more, and that if he would just tell us everything he knows...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Repeating something wrong a thousand times won't make it right!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you are adventurers with vast amounts of experience. And unlike that father-daughter pair, you have no link to this place... So, who do you think is right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! You can't just spring that on us!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: But no one here can really understand Benben.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if you asked us, we wouldn't be able to answer a question like that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Instead of worrying about differing opinions, why don't we focus our attention on a real problem! Like...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, didn't the stone slate light up earlier? But there are still so many blank spots on it! So, do you think we'll find clues about this stone slate here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Why don't we take a look at the stone slate, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! It's shining! Looks like it's opened up a new passageway, too!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: So it really is a key.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if you look closely, there still are empty patches! Hmm... Tirzad, can you tell us about the symbols on it now?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Uh... I'll have the answer once they're all lit up. It's still too early now. I can't jump to conclusions...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Haha, you know, that does make sense! If the people of the past were fond of using inverted sentences, we may come to a completely opposite conclusion if we don't have all the information.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, y'know, Paimon kinda doubts that would happen!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Ahem! Since the passageway to the next place has shown itself, we have no other choice but to push forward.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, will things really go that smoothly? Paimon keeps having the feeling that something is leading us forward...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Going back the way we came is an option...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: How can we turn back at this point? My masterpiece just needs some final touches! Just that tiny piece of decisive proof! I expect all of you to stay until the end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Should you really call a decisive piece of evidence tiny?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Paimon may not know whether Jebrael or Tirzad is correct, but we'll definitely get an answer if we continue, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's be more careful from now on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mhm! ...Hey! Wait a minute! Paimon hasn't said anything yet!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Hey, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, thank goodness! You're finally awake!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon doesn't know what happened either. We were here when Paimon woke up. Maybe it was a trap?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Anyway, let's go look for the others!

talks.objective: Find the members of the archaeology team

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: *sob* You're finally here! My savior!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I woke up to find myself in this place, and my whole body felt like it was falling apart...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: That wasn't even the end of it! I went to great lengths to finally find Jeht and her father, but the Fatui attacked again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! That's terrible!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Paimon, {NICKNAME}, did you see Benben on the way? B—Benben is gone! I searched all around the area to no avail...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We didn't, did we, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We didn't.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Then... Benben must be up ahead. It's the only one left alone now, so we must find it soon!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: There's no need to be so anxious. The way I see it, it probably only got lost because it likes running off by itself so much.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Benben has helped us so much! It's part of our group! I don't know about you, but I wouldn't be so cruel as to abandon a companion!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I must find Benben...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Its capabilities are undeniable, Tirzad. I'm sure you're aware of that.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Even you, Jebrael...?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Fine, you win! Let's find Benben first. But... I'm leaving if we encounter the Fatui again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, what are the Fatui doing here? Is this some kind of archaeological hotspot?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Huh? That's impossible! I wouldn't have chosen this place if it were such a hot research topic.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: True. After all, you've said yourself that you aren't a very great researcher.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You probably wouldn't stand a chance against those elites!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Hey! It's called avoiding battles where victory isn't guaranteed.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Either way, this place may be more troublesome than we expected. Let's advance carefully.

talks.objective: Proceed deeper within to find Benben
Proceed deeper within to find Benben
Proceed deeper within to find Benben
Proceed deeper within to find Benben

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: That room's... I wonder if it was a trap. Why did it send us here?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: It's common practice to attempt to expel trespassing outsiders. If you want technical details, you'll have to wait until I return and ask some Kshahrewar experts...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh, but I wonder: If King Deshret was a tyrant like you say, why wasn't that a lethal mechanism instead?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: We're just lucky that we haven't encountered one yet! And I hope that we never do...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Look! We can continue our expedition on this path. I don't want to give up when we've finally found some clues about the stone slate.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Shh... Those guys down there aren't friendly. We must find a way around them to proceed forward, or...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It's the Fatui and the Eremites again! Y'know, {NICKNAME}, Paimon's been thinking... Did they kidnap Benben?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: We've got to rescue it!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Jeht! Calm down.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Are you kidding? I'm just an ordinary researcher. I've come here to solve academic problems, not to fight!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we wouldn't have been able to get here without Benben... And Tirzad, you'll never be able to solve those academic problems of yours without Benben, either!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #That's right! We've got to rescue it, even if it's just for the sake of completing our expedition! You're not afraid of them, right, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Don't worry, {NICKNAME}'s an expert at dealing with the Fatui! But we should still be careful!

talks.objective: Go to the Fatui camp to search for clues

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Ha! I was wondering when you would get here, my dear Jebrael.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: And here you are, just as I expected, even without an invitation from me. Oh, how long has it been since we last spoke face-to-face?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Even my fingers on both hands aren't enough to count the years. What about you? Do you remember, Jebrael?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! That guy seems really strange! But it looks like he knows Jebrael?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: How cold. Is our reunion after so many years apart not worth a glass of wine and a toast?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: You know I don't hold the past against you. Either that, or I'm not "Samail the Straight Shooter"!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: There's still a place for you in Thutmose. Just say the word and everything can go back to how it was. Indeed, we can even go claim the debt that Babel owes us!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: ...I knew it! I knew Jebrael wasn't a good person! He's a—actually old friends with someone like this?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Nonsense! Father may have kept some things from me... B—But I believe he has his reasons.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Haha! That really hurts, Jeht.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Huh? How do you know my name?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: How could I not? Why, Jebrael, you've got such a cold heart! And it's "like father, like daughter," I see.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Ah, dear Jeht, you may have forgotten me. But luckily, I still remember it very well.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: I held you in my arms when you were just a little baby. With the moonlight on one side and the bonfire on the other, just like your parents...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: How come...

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: It seems like Jebrael didn't tell you anything at all, huh? Come on, that can't be! Jebrael, couldn't you even tell your own daughter the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Oh, well, I suppose I shouldn't have been too shocked. After all, we did call you the "Treacherous Grit."

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: As I listened to my subordinates reporting to me about the responses of the foreign merchants in the oasis, I started to wonder who gave them such wisdom, yet only instructed them without explaining anything at all.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: But even I could never have imagined that little Jeht's place in your heart is no different than those foreign merchants — mere strangers to you!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: You don't even dare to tell her about your past. Why? Are you afraid she'll hear about your history of betrayal and look down on you?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Samail... To be honest, I'm quite relieved to see that you're still the same lippy fellow I remember.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: ...Now, I have nothing to worry about if I beat you to the point where you'll leave of your own accord.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Haha! So you are afraid! You're afraid that this ghost of your past will seek you out for the debt you owe.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: But of course, I have the right! The secrets of Al-Ahmar belong to the Thutmose! Yet you took the "key" and betrayed us! You betrayed all of us grains of sand!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Just look at yourself! You're with children and cowards! Hah! Where's the ferocity you once had? Has it flowed away like sand flows out from between the fingers?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Enough! Hand Benben over.

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: "Benben"? Oh, that mechanical creation?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Hahahaha! Hey, did you all hear that? Jebrael actually calls this thing "Benben"!

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, these Snezhnayans aren't our old acquaintances, or this would be much, much more amusing.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Hand over Benben, or else...

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Or else what? Jebrael, is this even necessary? Ultimatum after ultimatum... Have you finally changed your mind? Do you plan to finally sit down and catch up with me?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: Oh, right, do you remember what happened to Ufairah? Haha, you haven't forgotten, right?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: It's fine. Even if you've forgotten, I can help you refresh your memories... Again and again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the heck is this guy saying?

dialogues.speaker: Samail
dialogues.text: We do have another way to communicate, don't we? Come on, Jeht, why don't you and that kid over there lend him a hand? After all, Jebrael is much weaker than he used to be!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, that guy Samail looks strong... But we have to give him a good thrashing so we can get Benben back!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Benben! Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Bee-eep! Beep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems fine, but a little sad?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Hey, Jebrael! Y—You'd better tell us the truth right this instant, or we'll have to go our separate ways!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Samail is clearly some manner of a villain... But he was being so friendly with you, and even with Jeht. So, are you... are you part of the same group?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I knew it... I knew it all along! You agreed to my commission without even asking about the details. It's because you had a plan, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: You plotted with Samail to trick a simple and ignorant researcher like me to uncover the secrets here for you!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: And even used your own daughter to gain my trust for the sake of that goal, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: And you, Jeht! That naivety and ignorance of yours was just a facade that Jebrael made you put on, wasn't it? And what an actress you were, indeed...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tirzad, you're too much! Paimon thinks that Jeht really was in the dark about this, but as for Jebrael...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: #Paimon! You too, {NICKNAME}! Wake up! It's my kindness and gullibility that made me fall for their lies. Don't follow in my footsteps!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? I'm no actress...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: And you, father! This isn't the time for secrets! I, too, want to know the truth...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I won't make excuses for my "betrayal," nor do I think that I made the wrong choice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, Paimon remembers Samail calling Jebrael something like that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Treacherous Grit."

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Yes, there's nothing to hide there. I was once one of the sand people, Thutmose. No matter what it was in the past, now...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Anyway, Samail is a madman through and through. He will stop at nothing to achieve his objectives.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was obvious enough...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: ...My wife, Jeht's mother, was killed by him.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So that's what happened... Is that why you never ever mentioned her?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Your mother... was a researcher too. If it wasn't for me, she would have had a brighter future...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: At least she wouldn't have lost her life at such a young age...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Tirzad.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Wh—What? I won't just believe a word you said.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: That's reasonable. It was I who concealed my motives, so I brought this upon myself.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Hmph! At least you've got some self-awareness!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: But no matter what, I'll protect you until this commission is over.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: No way! It's obvious that Samail has a bone to pick with you! If you stay with me... I don't want to be targeted by someone like that!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Tirzad, you're being stupid again. That's just an old grudge between them. His current priority is definitely King Deshret's treasures. Why would he have taken Benben otherwise?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So, he'd come for you even if my father wasn't here. After all, you have the key to solving everything.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: ...I do? Wait. The stone slate!?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: #Good thing I gave it to {NICKNAME} for safekeeping... I knew it wasn't something safe!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: It's not just the stone slate, but your intelligence too. The knowledge you possess as a researcher is something he covets.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I—I don't want to be targeted in a place like this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! You can rest at ease with us here!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: There's no time to lose. The longer we delay, the more time he'll have to prepare.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: He's like a viper crawling through the shadows, and his blades are like a viper's fangs. We cannot show any weakness to him... Otherwise, it'll lead to fatal consequences.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: ...I hope you'll keep your word.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, as far as Paimon is concerned, Paimon thinks that staying united is even more important now that we've finally gotten Benben back! Look! There's still a long way ahead, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it's strange. What's Samail doing here? What they want should be up there, right?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: I'm sure he has a plan. Or perhaps we missed some clues around here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, then we absolutely can't allow our differences to delay our expedition! Let's go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon will take the front! All of you, keep up!

choices.text: It'll be fine with Jebrael here.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Father won't lose to that guy, and we have me, too! I—I won't let Samail harm anyone again!

talks.objective: Investigate the room located deep within

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: This should be the last place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's take a look at the stone slate. If things go the same way as before, there may be clues about the stone slate here.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: This is...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It lit up as expected, and... there's a map?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tirzad, these symbols on the stone slate should be your area of expertise, right? So, isn't it time to give us an explanation?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Yes, these inscriptions are most likely texts of praise. Someone in an exalted position like King Deshret would naturally be fond of things like this.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Look! All these wonders are an attempt at whitewashing his rule.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whitewashing, you say... But Paimon remembers you saying something different earlier!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Rule by force," you said!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! You spoke of submission and terror before — and you sure sounded convinced then, too!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Wh—What do you mean? These are conclusions I came to after careful analysis and reasoning. Just look at it! What would it be if not an attempt at whitewashing?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: It's very common for rulers to sugar-coat all their deeds. Since this entire ruin was made by King Deshret, it's not that hard to imagine that this is its purpose, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Reflecting on your own shortcomings in your work... Well, we researchers do that.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Though they mostly just write a few hypocritical lines in the acknowledgments of a research paper and call it a day.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: And you know what? They're just pretending to be modest. Why would any academic really believe that they're incompetent, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, somehow Paimon gets the feeling that he's hurting himself with his own words there...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Ahem, I must admit that Jebrael's analysis did give me some inspirations...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But! An outstanding researcher should be able to accept the opinion of others when they are correct. Needless obstinacy will make it impossible to make an academic breakthrough! Don't you think so too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've said everything that can be said from either side. Is there even anything left for us to say?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And here we see the researcher's ability to twist facts in its natural habitat...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: It's nothing of the sort! This is the deepening of understanding! *sigh* Your inability to realize that shows that you still have a long way to go.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Speaking of ways, is the place marked on the map our next destination?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Yes, I think it's where all treasures meet, and all secrets end.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Of course, it will be the end of our grand adventure too, and the penultimate chapter of my masterpiece!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: While I really wish to obtain all the answers at this instant, my body is exhausted...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Nachtigal and the others are still at the oasis... Oh, right, Samail's subordinates reported to him about merchants. Do you think they were attacked?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Oh no! I almost forgot that!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I told them what to do if something like that happened, so they... should be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! That's a first. Paimon's never heard Jebrael sound so uncertain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, let's get back to Nachtigal's group as soon as we can then. It'll be bad if they are in hot water that they can't get themselves out of!

talks.objective: Investigate the container at the center of the room
